Updated read-through incorporating SLOOS:
- Policy/macro: The FOMC held at 5.25–5.50% and kept QT on track, acknowledging strong Q3 growth, still-elevated inflation, and uncertainty around policy lags—keeping a hawkish-leaning pause.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks reported broad-based net tightening in C&I and CRE standards, wider loan spreads, lower risk tolerance, and weaker loan demand. Consumer credit (credit cards, autos) also tightened with higher pricing and stricter nonprice terms. Drivers cited include higher funding costs, deposit outflows/liquidity positions, declines in market values of fixed-income assets, and concerns about credit quality/collateral values, especially in CRE. Foreign banks reported similar tightening.
- Implications: Surveyed tightening and weaker demand point to additional drag on business capex, hiring, and consumer durables, with elevated refinancing risk in CRE. This should aid disinflation but raises downside risks to growth and credit performance in leveraged segments. Net effect: tighter credit conditions are likely to amplify the Fed’s “higher-for-longer” stance.

Bottom line: While growth was strong and the Fed paused, the SLOOS signals more restrictive credit supply and softer demand ahead. That shifts the tone from slightly positive to slightly negative/guarded relative to the prior read.
